note: Aluminium chloride is a salt and is not a superconductor, and the paper concerns FeSe crystals.
The only BaCuS2 superconductivity paper (Chinese Phys. Lett. 2021, DOI 10.1088/0256-307x/38/1/017501) is a calculation that suggests superconductivity, and no measurement was found.

Noncentrosymmetric CaPtAs is superconducting with Tc of about 1.5 K (PRL 2020 abstract read, DOI verified); the earliest paper found is the arXiv preprint 1912.01993 (2019) with the journal version 10.1007/s11433-019-1488-5 published in 2020.
Bulk superconductivity with Tc = 2.0 K was reported for self-flux-grown CaBi2 single crystals in PCCP 2016 (DOI verified, abstract read); the cited 2019 paper treats it as known.

Zhu et al. 2019 (DOI verified) reports intrinsic bulk superconductivity below 1.178 K at ambient pressure in CaSn3; the earliest report found is Luo et al. 2015 (DOI 10.1039/c5tc02373d, verified) on CaSn3 single crystals, which claimed Tc 4.2 K that Zhu et al. attribute to surface Sn.

Landaeta et al. (PRX 2022) report Tc = 0.26 K for CeRh2As2 single crystals, and Khim et al. (Science 2021, doi 10.1126/science.abe7518) is the earliest report I found, so an earlier report may exist; the abstracts do not state the pressure, and pressure is known to suppress superconductivity in this compound.
The search returned only a review of ThCr2Si2 f-electron compounds, so the CeAg2Si2 superconductivity and its pressure condition could not be confirmed.
Takahashi et al. 2003 found no superconductivity in undoped CeRu2Si2 down to 170 microkelvin; the Ce(SiRu)2 note paper studies PuCoGa5.
Ce2O2Bi is an antiferromagnetic Kondo lattice (10.1016/j.jallcom.2020.155229) with no superconductivity reported.
Co3Sn2S2 is a ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal; the abstract reports no superconductivity.
Known van der Waals ferromagnet, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
Nakajima et al. (Sci. Adv. 2015) report superconductivity suppressed with rising de Gennes factor in the RPdBi family, but whether DyPdBi itself superconducts was not confirmed.
Cheng et al. 2021 (DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-26482-7) reports magnetism-induced topological transitions in EuAs3 with no superconductivity.
FeAsS is an arsenosulfide mineral with no reported superconductivity, and the first reader's paper concerns FeS.

Gou et al. report bulk superconductivity below 2.9 K in FeB4 single crystals made at high pressure, but Wang et al. (J. Materiomics 2015) found no superconductivity down to 2.5 K, so the result is disputed.
FeCl4 is a tetrachloroferrate anion or salt, not a superconductor; the paper is a review of organic charge-transfer solids.

Experimental HfV2Ga4 superconductivity is reported (Santos et al. 2018, DOI 10.1016/j.physleta.2018.02.018; Bhattacharyya et al. 2020, DOI 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.022001), but no read experimental abstract states a Tc; Ferreira et al. 2018 quotes Tc 4.1 K but is a calculation.
Orbital-ordered Mott insulator with no superconductivity reported; the input row had no DOI, so the search was on the formula.

LaRu2As2 superconductivity at 7.8 K was reported in Science Bulletin 2016 (DOI verified by Crossref); Tc is taken from the title because the abstract was not retrieved, and bulk character is not confirmed from text read.
Only LaNiC2 superconductivity was found (DOI 10.1103/physrevb.103.014511), a different stoichiometry; no report on La2Ni5C3 was located.
LaPtIn is reported not to superconduct down to 0.4 K in the 2021 LaPdIn paper (PRB 104, 024505).
No superconductivity report for LaNi was found; the superconducting La2Ni2In paper (DOI 10.1103/physrevb.102.165125) is a different compound.
Ferroelectric insulator and nonlinear optics material, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
Magnetic spin-liquid candidate insulator with no superconductivity; plainly not one, so no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
No abstract was found and no Nb3N5 superconductivity report surfaced in searches; the title concerns delta-NbN.

McGuire et al. (PRB 2016, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.93.064507) reports superconductivity in the Nb5Si3-xBx family at 5.8 to 7.8 K, but the abstract does not state the Nb5SiB2 composition, so it could not be confirmed.
The cited paper is titled 'Absence of superconductivity in NbB' (10.1103/physrevmaterials.1.044803) and attributes the observed superconductivity to a minority Nb-rich phase.
The Ir-based search found superconducting CeIr3 (2.5 K, ambient) but no NdIr3 report, so NdIr3 could not be assessed.
Superconductivity appears only in epitaxially strained RuO2 films (Uchida et al., PRL 2020, DOI 10.1103/physrevlett.125.147001), and bulk RuO2 is not reported superconducting.
The abstract reports superconductivity coexisting with ferromagnetism in SmN and SmN/GdN superlattices but does not say whether the sample is bulk or film.
The DFT study of SnSe2 and SnS2 under pressure measures no ambient-pressure superconductivity.
The abstract reports 2D superconductivity in SnSe2 only when induced by electrostatic gating in an electric-double-layer transistor, which is an excluded route.
Tetragonal SrPd2Bi2 (CaBe2Ge2-type polymorph) is superconducting at 2.0 K per this 2016 Inorganic Chemistry paper (DOI verified, abstract read); the monoclinic polymorph is not superconducting.
SrSn2As2 is superconducting only under pressure (Cao et al. 2024, doi 10.1002/apxr.202300149), not at ambient pressure.
No experimental superconductivity report for ThAu2Si2 was found; the only hits were a ThCr2Si2-type ab initio screen and an unrelated UAu2Si2 magnetism paper.
TiAu is an itinerant antiferromagnetic metal (Wolowiec et al. 2017, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.95.214403); no superconductivity is reported.
Searches found only first-principles studies of hexagonal W2N3 that do not discuss superconductivity, so nothing was established either way.
Pristine Y2O2Bi is nonsuperconducting; superconductivity appears only after oxygen incorporation (Sei et al. 2016, DOI 10.1021/jacs.6b05275).
No experimental paper on YCoC2 superconductivity was found; the 2019 APL topology paper only cites a reported Tc of 4.2 K and the originating paper was not located.

Hamamoto and Kitagawa 2018 (DOI verified) abstract gives Tc 6.4 K for parent Zr5Pt3 at ambient pressure; this is the earliest experimental report I found, though an older Mn5Si3-type superconductivity paper (Waterstrat et al. 1990, DOI 10.1016/0022-5088(90)90302-z) may cover Zr5Pt3 and its abstract was not available to read.
ZrNBr is superconducting only when electrostatically gated (Wang et al. 2019), not intrinsically at ambient pressure.
ZrSiS shows superconductivity only with a metallic silver tip on the surface, and high-pressure resistivity shows none up to about 20 GPa.
Undoped ZrTe2 becomes superconducting only under pressure (Zhu et al., Adv. Sci. 2023, DOI 10.1002/advs.202301332), and the superconducting Te-deficient ZrTe1.8 is a different composition.
Elemental silver is a normal metal at ambient pressure; the cited paper uses Ag only as an electrode (answered without search).
Al2O3 is an insulating substrate; the paper concerns proton irradiation of YBCO films.
The only AgAlO2 result is a first-principles prediction of Tc for hole-doped delafossites, with no measured superconductivity.
AlAuO2 is only a calculation-based design of a delafossite fermion system, with no measured superconductivity (answered without search).
The cited work is a calculation-only design of superconductivity in hole-doped CuAlO2 with no measured superconductivity (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
Only a 2026 electronic-structure study of AlNi3 turned up, with no superconductivity reported; the evidence is thin.
B2O3 is a glass-forming insulator and the cited paper is about boron doping of YBCO (answered without search).
Semiconductor, not a superconductor; the cited paper is about MgB2 films, which agrees with the first reader.
BaCr2As2 is an itinerant antiferromagnetic metal (Singh et al. 2009, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.79.094429; Filsinger et al. 2017, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.95.184414); no superconductivity is reported.
BaCu2As2 is a nonsuperconducting metal in the ThCr2Si2 form, and superconductivity was reported only under pressure in a different polymorph (Wu et al., APS abstract, 2021).
Ambient-pressure BaFe2As2 is not superconducting; superconductivity appears only under pressure (10.1103/physrevb.81.224511) or with doping, as in the cited work.
BaMn2As2 is an antiferromagnetic semiconductor (Singh et al. 2009, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.79.094519); superconductivity appears only as a pressure-based suggestion.
BaZn2As2 is a narrow-gap semiconductor (about 0.23 eV, 10.1021/ja507890u) and no superconductivity was found; the cited work is on diluted magnetic semiconductors.
BaF2 is an ionic fluoride used as a substrate, and the paper cited is about superconducting films on it.
BaNd2ZnO5 is studied for spin-chain frustration, not superconductivity (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
BaZrO3 is a perovskite oxide used as an insulator or substrate and is not a superconductor; the cited paper is about Dy123.
Bi2Rh3S2 shows a structural transition near 165 K and no superconductivity down to 0.5 K, with bulk superconductivity only in Bi2Rh3.5S2 (10.1103/physrevb.91.174513).
Binary BiS2 is not a known superconductor; the cited paper is on Sr0.5La0.5FBiS2 under pressure only.

No superconductivity report for the BiSe2 stoichiometry was found; the superconducting BiSe2-layer compound found is LaO0.5F0.5BiSe2, a different compound, and Bi2Se3 is superconducting only under pressure or after intercalation.
No ambient-pressure calcium superconductivity paper was retrieved, and the pressure reports were not reached, so the answer is not settled.
CaCo2As2 is studied as an antiferromagnet or metamagnet (for example 10.1103/physrevb.92.144416) and no superconductivity was reported in the papers found.
No superconductivity report for a calcium rhodium boride was found; searches returned only rare-earth Rh borides.
CaF2 is an insulating fluoride, and the paper treats it as a substrate for iron-based superconducting films.
CaMn7O12 is a multiferroic oxide with no superconductivity reported; the cited paper concerns BaFe2Se3 (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
The ruthenate studied shows metal-insulator transitions and magnetic order, with no superconductivity, per the first reader's note.
Semiconductor, not a superconductor; the cited chapter is about organic superconductors, which agrees with the first reader.
CePd2Ge2 is an antiferromagnet (TN 5.1 K) and no superconductivity is reported for it at ambient pressure in the papers found.
CeRu2Ge2 is a ferromagnetic heavy fermion; under pressure it becomes nonmagnetic near 10 GPa with no superconductivity down to 60 mK (10.1103/physrevb.57.5025).

CeNi2As2 in the ThCr2Si2 form is an antiferromagnet (TN 4.8 K) per Luo et al. 2012, and an unreviewed 2026 preprint reports superconductivity in the CaBe2Ge2-type polymorph, so the structure of this record cannot be settled.
CeO2 is a nonsuperconducting oxide and the record had no title or DOI; no CeO2 superconductivity paper was found.
Not searched directly; the related ZrCuSiAs-type phosphide oxide hits report no superconductivity but do not cover this composition, so the answer is not settled.
Searches on CePdSb returned no superconductivity report, but no paper on this compound could be read.
Spinel insulator, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
No report of superconductivity in CoAs3 was found in the searched literature.
CoPt is a ferromagnet; the superconductivity reported (Rakshit et al. 2008, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.77.094505) is of NbN in NbN-CoPt film bilayers.
Magnetic CoPt3 nanocrystal study on superparamagnetism; no superconductivity reported (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
CrO2 is a ferromagnet; the paper is on percolation in MgB2 and CrO2 nanocomposites.
Cs2Se is an ionic salt, and the first reader's paper is a review of iron-based superconductors rather than this compound.
No superconductivity report for CsCSN was found; the paper on CaIrSi3 is a different compound.
Cesium sulfide is an ionic salt and not a superconductor in its own right.
Elemental dysprosium is an antiferromagnet at ambient pressure and not a superconductor (answered without search).

Tsvyashchenko et al. 2013 (DOI verified, title matches) abstract states that EuFe2As2 polycrystals synthesized at 8 GPa show superconductivity with Tc 20-30 K at ambient pressure, but zero resistance was not observed, so this is a weak claim; Miclea 2009 and Terashima 2009 report superconductivity only under pressure.
The EuFe2P2 study (DOI 10.1103/physrevb.82.094426) reports ferromagnetic and Kondo behavior with no superconductivity.
Well-known ferromagnetic insulator, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
No superconductivity reported for EuP in the literature found; the cited paper concerns iron pnictides, so this agrees with the first reader.
EuS is a ferromagnetic semiconductor and the cited paper is on spin-polarized tunneling with no superconductivity (answered without search).
Known magnetic semiconductor, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
Elemental fluorine is a gas, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
FeCo is a ferromagnetic alloy and the cited theory concerns a trilayer in which FeCo is a magnetic layer (answered without search).
Co2FeSi-type magnetic compound, not a superconductor; the cited paper is on Co2FeSi-NbN bilayers (answered without search).
FeNi is a magnetic alloy; the paper is on magneto-optics of irradiated Ba(Fe,M)2As2.
FePd appears only as a magnetic layer in Nb/FePd heterostructures, and no superconductivity in FePd itself was reported.
No report of superconductivity in the FeSe2 pyrite phase was found; the closest match (DOI 10.1021/acs.inorgchem.8b03089) reports a spin-glass Fe-Pd-Se phase.
Elemental gadolinium is not superconducting at ambient pressure, and the paper concerns rare-earth ruthenocuprates.
No superconductivity report for GdCo2B2 itself was found, and the borocarbide reviews cover only nearby compositions.
GdCl3 appears only as a parameter set in a spin-wave paper; it is a magnetic salt and not a superconductor.
No superconductivity report for Ge2Pt (PtGe2) was found; the only related paper found is on the BaPt4Ge12 skutterudite.
Insulating nitride, not a superconductor; no search was run, and the cited paper is about LaFeAsO, which agrees with the first reader.
Undoped HfNCl is an insulator; superconductivity appears only after electron doping by intercalation (Yamanaka et al. 1998, DOI 10.1038/33362; Felser and Seshadri 1999, DOI 10.1039/a808127a).
HgBr2 is a salt and the cited tunneling study concerns Bi-2212, which is the superconductor (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
Semiconductor; superconductivity appears only in Nb/InAs junctions, an induced effect, so this agrees with the first reader.
Tissen et al. 1998 reports superconductivity of InBi only as a function of pressure up to 40 GPa; no ambient-pressure superconductivity is reported in the paper found.
K2Se is not a known superconductor; the cited paper is on phase relations in KxFe2-ySe2 (answered without search).
KP(HO2)2 is KH2PO4 (KDP), a dielectric crystal whose pressure effects on permittivity were studied, with no superconductivity.
Insulating perovskite; superconductivity is reported only at interfaces or in doped forms, so bulk KTaO3 is not a superconductor here.
LaCo2P2 is a weak itinerant ferromagnet with no superconductivity reported, which agrees with the first reader.
Insulating oxide, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
LaAlO3 is only the substrate in the LaFeAsO films paper.
A neutron diffraction study of LaCrSb3 itself reports coexisting magnetic orders and no superconductivity, which agrees with the first reader.
Searches found superconductivity in La3Pt4 below 0.51 K and in LaPt2-based phases, but no report on the 1:1 LaPt composition.
LaZnAsO is a semiconductor (gap about 1.5 eV, 10.1021/ja507890u) and the cited paper is on diluted magnetic semiconductors; no superconductivity was found.

Tuoriniemi et al. (Nature 2007, DOI verified by verify_reference) title reports superconductivity in lithium below 0.4 millikelvin at ambient pressure, which contradicts the note's pressure-only claim; the Tc was read from the title because the abstract was not retrieved, and the 2004 PRL on this topic only gives an upper limit.
Only theory was found: LiB is computed to be an insulator, and an older calculation expects at best low-temperature superconductivity, with no measured superconductivity.
LiBC is reported as a semiconductor from optical and dielectric measurements, with no superconductivity.
Only first-principles calculations of Li-graphene systems were found, with no measured superconductivity in LiC.
Searched only LiC6-type intercalation results, which do not establish a superconducting LiC12 phase, so the answer is not settled.
A review chapter states that KC8 is a superconductor and LiC6 is not, so the lithium graphite intercalation compound is not superconducting at ambient pressure.
LiFeO2 is only the spacer block in (LiFeO2)Fe2Se2 and is not reported superconducting (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
Searches found only lutetium hydride papers and no experimental report of superconductivity in elemental Lu at ambient pressure, so none could be verified.
Elemental magnesium is not a superconductor at ambient pressure, and the paper concerns superconductivity at a metal-oxidized Mg interface.
Carbon-substituted MgB2 is reported superconducting only for carbon fractions up to about 0.15, and no report was found at the Mg(BC)2 composition (x = 0.5).
MgAl2O4 is a spinel insulator and substrate; the paper is about superconducting spinel oxide thin films.
The only superconducting Mg-Ir-B phase found is Mg12-dIr19B16 (Tc 5.7 K, PRB 2007), a different stoichiometry, and no report on the 1:1:1 phase was found.
Insulating oxide used as a substrate, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
Mn(CrS2)2 (MnCr2S4) is a thiospinel half-metallic antiferromagnet; the abstract reports no superconductivity.
Mn3GaC is studied for electronic structure and antiferromagnetic nesting with no superconductivity (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
MnGa is a ferromagnetic compound, and the first reader's paper concerns ferromagnetism in ion-implanted (Ga,Mn)P.
MnGaNi2 is a ferromagnetic Heusler alloy; the abstract covers its order-disorder transition and no superconductivity.
MnSi is a well-known helimagnet; the quantum phase transition review does not show superconductivity in MnSi.
Superconductivity in NaCl-type MoN was reported only in films (10.1088/0305-4608/14/7/005, 10.1103/physrevb.73.052504), not in bulk samples.
Nitrogen is a gas, and the paper concerns MgB2 thin films.
Elemental sodium becomes superconducting only at very high pressure, and the paper cited is a Hubbard-model study of carbon nanotubes.

Parker et al. 2009 (DOI 10.1039/b818911k) reports superconductivity coexisting with magnetic order in NaFeAs, but the abstract read gives no Tc and the DOI was not run through verify_reference, so no yes can be given.
NaVO3 is an oxide insulator; the paper is a spin-isospin model of NaV2O5.
Elemental neodymium is a magnetic metal with no ambient-pressure superconductivity reported; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
NdNi5 is a magnetic intermetallic with no reported bulk superconductivity, so the first reader's note stands.
Elemental nickel is not superconducting at ambient pressure, and the paper concerns the cuprate YBa2Cu4O8 with Ni as a dopant.
NiS2 is a pyrite-type Mott insulator, and the first reader's paper shows only its magnetic phase diagram and metal-insulator transition.
NpO2 is an actinide oxide; the paper is on multipole Coulomb interactions and magnetic moments, with no superconductivity.
PrRu2Si2 is a magnetic compound with a crystal-field ground state (Mulders et al., PRB 1997), and no superconductivity was reported.
Searches found no PuGa3 superconductivity; the Pu superconductors retrieved are PuCoGa5 and PuRhGa5, and the cited paper reports none for PuGa3.
Si3N4 is an insulator and the cited paper is a theory of topological insulator and superconductor interplay (answered without search).
SiO2 is only the substrate in the TaN thin-film paper.
No superconductivity reported for SmSI; the cited paper is a calculation on TiNCl-type layered nitrides (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
SrCo2As2 is a nonsuperconducting paramagnetic metal at ambient pressure (10.1103/physrevb.91.220406), and the cited paper concerns only a pressure-induced collapsed-tetragonal phase.
Sr2YRuO6 is studied as an insulating magnet from band calculations with no superconductivity (answered from the first reader note, not searched).

Pure Sr3Ru2O7 has not been reported superconducting (Kittaka et al. PRB 2008, doi 10.1103/physrevb.77.214511), and a later preprint finds none down to 15 mK, while apparent superconductivity appears only in Sr2RuO4-intergrown eutectic crystals.
Substrate material for film growth, not a superconductor; no search was run, and this agrees with the first reader.
This manganite shows magnetic relaxation, and the first reader's note found no superconductivity indicated.
SrRuO3 is an itinerant ferromagnet and the cited paper is a Stoner-theory calculation with no superconductivity (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
Only a 1980 title on SrSi2 superconductivity (Evers et al., DOI 10.1016/0022-5088(80)90297-0) was found, with no abstract read; SrSi does not match the SrSi2 stoichiometry.
Kaczorowski et al. (arXiv cond-mat/0103571) abstract reports Tc 9.5 K, but that DOI is not registered with Crossref, and other 2001 TaB2 studies found no superconductivity down to 1.5 K.
No TaInS2 superconductivity report was found; the cited paper concerns PbTaSe2 and searches returned only TaS2 and TaB2 results.
Searches returned no bulk TaN superconductivity paper, only the film work the first reader noted, so the bulk question could not be settled.

Machado et al. report Th2NiC2 as a new bulk superconductor, with Tc 11.2 K for the Sc-substituted Th1.8Sc0.2NiC2, and the undoped phase is quoted at Tc 8.5 K in a later abstract (Quan and Pickett 2013).
Searches for Ti2N and TiN bulk superconductivity returned only MXene and calculation papers, with no measured superconductivity.
TiO2 is a wide-gap oxide insulator and is not superconducting.
UCoGa5 is a Pauli paramagnet that is not superconducting above 0.3 K, and the superconductor in this family is PuCoGa5.
USe is a magnetic actinide chalcogenide named only as an example in a theory of itinerant ferromagnetism.
XeF2 is a fluorinating gas reagent; the paper is on Bi2(O,F)S2 superconductors.
Elemental yttrium is superconducting only under high pressure (Hamlin et al., PRB 2006, DOI 10.1103/physrevb.73.094522), and no ambient-pressure report was found.
Only the carbide YNi2B2C is superconducting at ambient pressure; the boride YNi2B2+x was reported superconducting only as high-pressure phases.
The cited work is on yttrium substitution in La1-xYxO0.5F0.5BiS2; Y2SO2 is not reported superconducting (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
Only ab initio papers on Lu2Ni3Si5 and Y2Ni3Si5 were found, and no measurement of superconductivity in Y2Ni3Si5 was located.

Takei et al. 1986 (DOI 10.1016/0022-5088(86)90098-6) has a title claiming superconducting properties of YRh3B, but no abstract giving a Tc was available; the 2006 Sc3XB paper only compares with YRh3B.

Radmanesh et al. report superconductivity in YPdBi single crystals with Tc about 1 K, and the earliest report I found is the 2015 Nakajima et al. RPdBi family paper, whose abstract does not name YPdBi explicitly.
NQR and NMR on YCoGe show conventional metallic behaviour and no superconducting transition down to 0.3 K (JPSJ 2011, doi 10.1143/jpsj.80.064711).
The cited superconductivity is interface superconductivity in strained topological crystalline insulators, not bulk YbS (answered from the first reader note, not searched).
ZnO is a wide-gap semiconductor and the cited paper reports ferromagnetism, not superconductivity (answered without search).
No superconductivity report for the ZrCuSiAs compound itself was found; the ZrCuSiAs-type results are for doped or other members of the structure family.
